searchText: To be clear, for pectra OP Stack has already done the scrambling and prepped to make sure we’ll be ready for the originally proposed mainnet dates. So given things shifted back a week we don’t need to increase the notice period for this particular fork. But I do think that as a general rule, it’s important to actually be code complete in clients with a stable spec before trying to set dates because downstream folk depend on that before we can really get busy testing and pulling in upstream changes to clients etc. Also it’s not great engineering practice to try and squeeze testing to make a date - that just reduces quality and increases risk. As many have pointed out, having a smaller scope and fixing that scope earlier is a much safer way to accelerate timelines and it delivers much greater results as it can shave months off instead of a week here or there. And as mentioned above I think L1 should set an example for others in terms of the amount of notice given to users to allow them to exit if desired before an upgrade activates. I don’t mind what that timeline is exactly but we should line it up with things like the stage 2 definition for L2s and whatever other best practices there are for app platforms. All of this makes sense to me, but I will say that people working on rollups have expressed to me that “every day matters” in how soon we ship, so getting a more “unified” perspective from L2 teams about the right delays would be great! Might be a good topic for RollCall? If there was an immutable OP Stack L2, would 7702 brick it? Yes. An upgrade is needed for compatibility with pectra I loved this argument by Adrian I think both things can be true. In an ideal world pectra would already have shipped with a good long notice period. That would require changing something much earlier in the process - likely cutting scope or finalizing scope earlier. I’ve been around enough to know that’s not easy and not always possible. I’m not asking to delay this release. OP stack doesn’t currently have a forced 30 day delay for upgrades so we can update quickly and it will all work out. Going forward there’s lots of pressure to keep moving towards stage 2 which does require long enforced upgrade delays. We can’t do that if L1 is shipping upgrades with a shorter notice period. We want to enable trust reducing features like long upgrade delays in lots of places through the ecosystem so we need to move L1 development towards better supporting it. That's fair, but I do think it'd be nice to then have the L2s come to conensus about what the rollout timeline should be for upgrades. I think ACD is largely ambivalent towards that and so the guidance would be useful 🙂 Also fair. For L2s I’d look to the definition of a stage 2 roll up. While these definitions do change a bit I think typically a 30 day upgrade delay. If there is an expectation that stuff built on Ethereum will need to change when Ethereum hard forks, then I feel like we have a pretty big problem as stuff deployed immutably to Ethereum should work indefinitely. It is concerning that OP Stack will break because of a new transaction type. I don't know why this would be the case, but it seems like L2s should be resilient to changes in L1 block shape and transaction types, as long as old transactions types remain supported. ~~<@&595685821026271242> https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/1335077641132445716~~ deleted, not sure if by mod or scammer. Immutability Changes to data structures break merkle proofs on the light client, and there's no way to prevent that. So I'm not sure this is a valid argument. obligatory SSZ stablecontainer 🤷‍♀️ I don't understand? You can prevent it by stopping changes to L1. 😄 Alternatively, using datastructures that can be proven in a backward compatible way. for example https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7688 https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-7807.md etc there's a whole cluster of these EIPs on which <@881905303011086387> is working That's not enough, correct fork version needs to be mixed in as well. Will have a look though. https://stabilitynow.box/ is probably the best overview/summary Would solve for ssz structures yeah but the sync committee signatures relying on the fork version would still be a problem

If there is an expectation that stuff built on Ethereum will need to change when Ethereum hard forks, then I feel like we have a pretty big problem as stuff deployed immutably to Ethereum should work indefinitely.

It is concerning that OP Stack will break because of a new transaction type.  I don't know why this would be the case, but it seems like L2s should be resilient to changes in L1 block shape and transaction types, as long as old transactions types remain supported.
